questions.q: What is the actual error in this lesson's cash receipt scenario?
options: Harborview's payment was deposited to the wrong bank account
The receipt amount does not match any invoice on Harborview's account
The $55,100.00 receipt was applied to the smaller, unrelated INV-HV-29890 instead of INV-HV-30144
The receipt was never recorded in Oracle Fusion at all
questions.explain: Mateo Rios applies the $55,100.00 receipt to the older $6,100.00 invoice, INV-HV-29890, instead of the matching $55,100.00 invoice, INV-HV-30144.

questions.q: What does INV-HV-29890 show after the misapplication?
options: A $49,000.00 credit (overpaid) balance
A $6,100.00 balance, unchanged
It is automatically closed and removed from the account
A $55,100.00 open balance
questions.explain: Applying the $55,100.00 receipt to the $6,100.00 invoice leaves it with a $49,000.00 credit balance — overpaid far beyond its actual value.

questions.q: What happens to the total cash balance and total AR control account balance because of this misapplication?
options: Both are overstated by $49,000.00
Both are understated by $55,100.00
Neither is affected — only the invoice-level open-item detail is wrong
Cash is understated, but AR is unaffected
questions.explain: The GL impact of the receipt itself is correct in total; the misapplication only moves which invoice shows as paid versus open, not the overall balances.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a misapplied receipt is invisible in a bank reconciliation or trial balance?
options: Because the receipt was never actually deposited
Because bank reconciliation and the trial balance work at a summary/cash level, while the error exists only in invoice-level AR aging detail
Because Oracle Fusion automatically hides misapplied receipts from reports
Because the customer's account is excluded from both reports
questions.explain: Since total cash and total AR are unaffected, the error only becomes visible in detailed, invoice-by-invoice AR aging — not in summary-level reconciliations.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion allow the receipt to be applied to an invoice of a different amount?
options: It doesn't — Oracle Fusion blocks any mismatch between receipt and invoice amount
Because applying a receipt to a specific invoice is a valid instruction regardless of whether the amounts match
Because INV-HV-29890 was flagged as the default invoice for all receipts
Because receipts can only be applied to the single oldest invoice on an account
questions.explain: Nothing in Receivables requires a receipt's amount to match the invoice it's applied to — it's a valid, if mistaken, user instruction.
